newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-PASSARELLA TAKES ANOTHER SWIPE AT THE COPA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PASSARELLA TAKES ANOTHER SWIPE AT THE COPA.

text.p: Argentina coach Daniel Passarella took another swipe at the Copa America on Monday.
"The circus carries on, business as well, and the players never get a rest," he said. "It would be better to stop playing football for a while, then it might become better to watch."

Passarella has been one of the most outspoken critics of the fact that the Copa America and the region's World Cup qualifying matches have clashed. Argentina are one of several countries who have responded by bringing B teams to the Copa America.
"There are players here who have had seven or eight days' holiday all year yet they are still expected to give their all every time they take the field," he said.
Passarella is also against the marathon format for the South American World Cup qualifying matches in which the nine countries play each other twice.
The fixture list is tough on South America's European-based players, who are forced to play key international games when their club colleagues are having a few weeks in the sun.
